data.q: Which Visual Studio edition is free for individual developers, open source projects, and small teams?
data.e: Visual Studio Community is free for individual developers, open source projects, academic research, education, and small professional teams (up to 5 users).

data.q: What is the primary difference between Visual Studio and Visual Studio Code?
o: VS Code is a full IDE; Visual Studio is a lightweight editor
Visual Studio is a full-featured IDE; VS Code is a lightweight, extensible code editor
They are identical but with different branding
VS Code only supports C#; Visual Studio supports all languages
data.e: Visual Studio is a comprehensive IDE with built-in tools for debugging, profiling, designers, and ALM. VS Code is a lightweight editor that becomes powerful through extensions.

data.q: Which command creates a new console application in the current directory using the .NET CLI?
data.e: `dotnet new console` creates a new console project. Use `-o` or `--output` to specify a directory.

data.q: In Visual Studio, which window shows the hierarchical structure of your solution, projects, and files?
data.e: Solution Explorer displays the solution tree with projects, references, NuGet packages, and files. Class View shows code elements (classes, methods).

data.q: What is the name of the C# extension for Visual Studio Code maintained by Microsoft?
data.e: The official Microsoft extension is simply named 'C#' (published by Microsoft). C# Dev Kit is a separate extension that adds project management and testing UI. OmniSharp is the language server powering the C# extension.

data.q: Which file format does Visual Studio use to store solution metadata?
data.e: .sln (solution) files organize multiple projects. .csproj is for C# projects, .vbproj for VB.NET, .fsproj for F#.

data.q: How do you install a NuGet package in Visual Studio Code using the .NET CLI?
data.e: `dotnet add package` adds a NuGet package reference to the project file. The NuGet CLI (`nuget.exe`) is separate and not typically used in VS Code workflows.

data.q: Which debugging feature allows you to execute code line by line and inspect variable values at runtime?
data.e: Breakpoints pause execution. Watch window monitors expressions. Immediate window evaluates expressions and executes statements. All are core debugging features in both VS and VS Code.

data.q: What is the purpose of the `launch.json` file in a VS Code workspace?
data.e: launch.json defines debug configurations (e.g., .NET Core Launch, Attach to Process). It lives in the .vscode folder.

data.q: Which Visual Studio feature provides real-time collaborative editing and debugging with team members?
data.e: Visual Studio Live Share enables real-time collaborative editing, debugging, and terminal sharing. It works across VS and VS Code.

data.q: What does the `dotnet restore` command do?
data.e: `dotnet restore` restores NuGet packages defined in the project file. It runs implicitly on `dotnet build` and `dotnet run` but can be called explicitly.

data.q: In Visual Studio, which build configuration is typically used for development and debugging?
data.e: Debug configuration includes full debug symbols, no optimization, and defines DEBUG constant. Release enables optimizations and defines TRACE.

data.q: Which testing framework is built into .NET and supported natively by Visual Studio and VS Code?
data.e: All three are supported. MSTest is Microsoft's framework; xUnit and NUnit are popular third-party frameworks with first-class tooling support.

data.q: What is the purpose of the `global.json` file in a .NET solution?
o: Pins the .NET SDK version for the solution
data.e: global.json specifies the .NET SDK version to use, ensuring consistent builds across machines and CI pipelines.

data.q: Which Visual Studio window shows memory usage, CPU utilization, and other performance metrics during debugging?
data.e: Diagnostic Tools (Debug > Windows > Show Diagnostic Tools) provides real-time performance profiling during debugging sessions.

data.q: How do you enable .NET hot reload in Visual Studio Code?
o: It is not supported in VS Code
data.e: `dotnet watch` enables hot reload for code changes during development. In VS, it's integrated via the 'Hot Reload' button; in VS Code, use the terminal.

data.q: What is the default terminal shell used by Visual Studio Code on Windows?
data.e: VS Code defaults to PowerShell on Windows. You can change it via `terminal.integrated.defaultProfile.windows` in settings.json.
